newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin says two-tier baht market temporary.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin says two-tier baht market temporary.

text.p: Thailand's Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Sunday that the current two-tier market for baht trading was temporary and aimed at protecting national interest.

Under the current informal two-tier system for baht trading which came about after the central bank cut off baht supply to offshore players 10 days ago following a speculative attack, there are effectively two rates quoted for the baht/dollar.
One rate is quoted locally while the other is quoted offshore and foreign players have to pay higher rates.

"We need an effective monetary system to facilitate our business. Currently there is a two-tier market because the Bank of Thailand is exercising measures to protect the country from outside threat," Amnuay told reporters.
"This measure should be temporary, while more long term and effective measures are being formulated. But we have no idea of creating multiple systems," he added.
The two-tier system came about after the last speculative attack on the baht.

Amnuay's statement contrasted sharply with that made earlier on Sunday by the head of the Thai Bankers Association, Olarn Chaiprawat who believed a formal two-tier market was likely for baht trading in the future.

Olarn said that the central bank was expected to come up with new measures to formally separate the offshore and onshore foreign exchange markets and he downplayed concerns that such a system could affect capital inflows needed to finance Thailand's current account deficit.

The Bank of Thailand is due to hold a press conference on Monday to announced unspecified monetary measures and guidelines for new consolidations in the financial sector after the collapse of the planned mega-merger between finance company Finance One Plc and Thai Danu Bank Plc.
